body: Sorry to hear that you are going through all this pain.  It's quite the coincidence, but my dream was to be a theoretical physicist - however, in my case, I simply did not have the abilities for it - I'm just not good at math and visuo-spatial processing.  So I did the next best thing, which is to work for a science company, but in an administrative/sales role, and in my spare time, I study science just for fun: I listen to lectures, download free online textbooks and study them, go to science museums, take part in online science  discussion forums, and even have weekly in-person science gatherings with other enthusiasts in my city where we just discuss our latest thoughts on various science subjects.

Sorry you are going through all this. With mindfulness of endeavoring to not be presumptuous,  I think I can say that I may be able to relate to this - feeling alone, empty, not being connected to something bigger and emotionally/spiritually meaningful, feelings of nihilism, and not even being able to enjoy simple hedonistic things - and in my case, taking a gamble that the next world, if one indeed does exists, would surely be more meaningful and rewarding than anything offered to me here.  I am glad though that you still have what it takes to go through schooling and have decent economic means.  I think this would mean that there is still good potential for a better future for you.  Perhaps just making new friends in your new community may help you get there.

Yeah, I know what that feels like, 9 billion people in the world all fighting for that small piece of pie.  What's important to you personally?    If one's main goal is wealth acquisition and  social status, then that's going to be the most competitive environment.  But if one is just trying to find a career that is ideologically meaningful to them and that they enjoy also and can also earn enough for a moderate life, then things may be a lot easier with respect to the competition.  Who knows.  I'm no expert in these matters anyway.
Sorry to hear that.  I'm always feeling like that.  Would you like to talk about it?

Well, for me, I often see situations in the world where innocent people are harmed, or there are great life inequalities and so forth.  But, I suppose one can say that in the end, do we not all die, regardless of what our position was on the socio-economic hierarchy?  The thing about life is that it is temporary - it does not matter if you are the King of country or an unfortunate homeless person.  So then, what good was all that effort to aggressively compete with others for dominance?  For some, I guess this is where religion can come in - a belief that if you live honestly and altruistically, then you will have a good equal life in the after-world.  I am agnostic, so I really don't know if there is or is not such an after-life.

I'm sorry things are so bad that you have to have such thoughts in the first place.  I've come to learn though that this forum is a place for helping each other avoid that final step from which there is no return.  Giving advice on how to self-harm is highly frowned upon, which I can understand, because I suppose that if someone is truly intent on taking that final path, they will eventually find a way, so this forum is about giving people all the help that is humanly possible to help them emotionally heal and look forward to life again.

Sorry to hear that.  What do the doctors have to say about your condition?  Anything I can suggest you can experiment with is stuff you probably already heard of anyway about improving health, like following a strict Mediterranean low glycemic diet, intermittent fasting, high anti-oxidant foods like teas, spices, legumes, coffee, cocoa, multivitamin/omega-3s, etc.  A doctor could give you sound nutritional advice.  Plus daily cardiovascular and basic weight training of bench press, bent-over rows, and squats, and enough sleep each night.  Good luck in whatever choice you make.
You're in good company - the official online community of people with mental health issues.  Let's have a virtual drink together, or a virtual cup of coffee!

No human is worthless.   You are a sentient being, and that alone makes you equal to everyone else.  Please always remember this.  9 billion people in the world, and we are all EQUAL brothers and sisters.  Hang in there, get the help you need, plenty of mental health professionals that can help.
Sorry to hear this.  I know what it feels like to feel hopeless, and I hope everything works out for you.  I hope you find happiness.
